title: Dynamic Hotel Pricing at Online Travel Platforms: A Popularity and Competitiveness Aware Demand Learning Approach

problem.claim: Hotel room demand on online booking platforms fluctuates with hotel popularity and competition, creating a need for dynamic pricing based on changing demand.

gap.claim: Room-level occupancy prediction is affected by data sparseness, and existing demand modeling needs to account for popularity and competitiveness while remaining interpretable and accurate.

contributions.claim: A dynamic pricing approach uses popularity- and competitiveness-aware demand learning.
A demand function incorporates popularity and competitiveness coefficients to model price elasticity of demand.
A multi-task dynamic demand prediction network learns the coefficients and leverages demand correlations among similar hotel groups to address room-level data sparseness.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the demand function incorporating popularity and competitiveness coefficients as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets reportedly show superiority over state-of-the-art baselines in demand prediction and dynamic pricing.
The model was reportedly deployed on an online travel platform serving tens of millions of users and hoteliers.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dynamic pricing is motivated by changing demand, and hotel demand varies with popularity and competition.
The paper proposes popularity- and competitiveness-aware demand learning for dynamic pricing.
The approach introduces a coefficient-based demand function and a network that learns its coefficients.
A multi-task framework uses correlations among similar hotels to mitigate room-level data sparseness.
The authors report improvements on real-world datasets and deployment on a large online travel platform.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset identities, sample sizes, time periods, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not identify the baselines or quantify the reported improvements.
The abstract does not describe the deployment period, operational constraints, or business outcomes.
